def: To leave your bed after sleeping.
ex: I usually get up at six on weekdays.
nat: Why did you get up so early today?
contrast: get up (sair da cama) ≠ wake up (acordar): I woke up at five but got up at six.

def: To have a friendly relationship with someone.
ex: I get along well with my new teammates.
nat: Do your kids get along with each other?

def: To recover from an illness or a bad experience.
ex: It took her months to get over the flu.
nat: You will get over it soon; just give it time.
contrast: get over (superar) ≠ get over with (acabar logo com algo desagradável).

def: To do something wrong without being punished.
ex: He thought he could get away with cheating on the test.
nat: You will not get away with this!

def: To manage to live or cope with limited money or resources.
ex: We can get by on one salary for a while.
nat: My Spanish is basic, but I can get by when I travel.

def: To finish or survive a difficult task or period.
ex: I need coffee to get through this meeting.
nat: Somehow we will get through this quarter.
contrast: get through (to someone) também significa conseguir contato: I couldn't get through to the helpline.

def: To contact someone later with an answer or information.
ex: Let me check and get back to you tomorrow.
nat: She promised to get back to me by Friday.
contrast: get back to (retornar o contato) ≠ come back to (voltar a um lugar).

def: To find a way to avoid a problem or rule.
ex: We can get around the delay by using express shipping.
nat: Is there any way to get around this error?
contrast: get around também = espalhar-se: News gets around fast.

def: To make an idea understood by other people.
ex: It was hard to get across how serious the problem was.
nat: Good presenters know how to get across complex ideas simply.

def: To refuse an offer or request.
ex: She turned down the job because the salary was too low.
nat: I had to turn down their invitation.
contrast: turn down também = abaixar o volume: Turn down the music.

def: To arrive or appear, often unexpectedly.
ex: Only half of the guests turned up on time.
nat: My keys turned up in the washing machine.
contrast: turn up (aparecer) é inseparável; turn up the volume (aumentar) é separável (turn it up) ≠ turn down.

def: To end up in a particular way.
ex: The weather turned out better than expected.
nat: It turns out that the bug was in the database.
contrast: turn out to be + substantivo/adjetivo: It turned out to be a mistake.

def: To change and become something different.
ex: The small startup turned into a global company.
nat: Water turns into ice below zero degrees.

def: To stop a machine or light from working.
ex: Please turn off your phones during the meeting.
nat: I always turn off my laptop before leaving.
contrast: turn off (desligar) ≠ turn someone off (tirar o interesse de alguém).

def: To make a machine, light or feature start working.
ex: Can you turn on the air conditioning? It is hot.
nat: The app asks you to turn on notifications.

def: To change direction, or to improve a bad situation.
ex: The new CEO managed to turn around the struggling company.
nat: We missed the exit and had to turn around.

def: To prepare or arrange something so it is ready to use.
ex: IT will set up your laptop on your first day.
nat: We set up a call with the vendor for Thursday.
contrast: set up (verbo) ≠ setup (substantivo): The setup took an hour.

def: To begin a journey.
ex: We set off at dawn to avoid the traffic.
nat: They set off for Lisbon early on Saturday.
contrast: set off (alarme/bomba) = disparar e é separável: The smoke set off the alarm / set it off.

def: To begin a task with a specific aim, or to present clearly.
ex: She set out to build a business of her own.
nat: The report sets out our main goals for next year.
contrast: set out to + verbo = ter como objetivo.

def: To save or keep something for a special purpose.
ex: I set aside an hour every day for studying.
nat: We need to set aside some budget for training.

def: To delay progress or cost someone a lot of money.
ex: The server crash will set back the launch by two weeks.
nat: Delays like this can set back the whole schedule.
contrast: set back também = custar: That repair set me back $500.

def: To start doing something with energy and purpose.
ex: He set about fixing the broken pipeline right away.
nat: How do you set about learning a new language?

def: To delay something until a later time.
ex: We had to put off the meeting until Monday.
nat: Don't put off calling the client any longer.
contrast: put off (delay) ≠ put off someone (discourage): The smell put me off.

def: To dress yourself in clothing or add something to your body.
ex: It is cold outside, so put on a jacket.
nat: She put on her glasses to read the contract.
contrast: put on weight = engordar; put on a show = encenar.

def: To accept something unpleasant without complaining.
ex: I can't put up with this noise any longer.
nat: He put up with long commutes for years.

def: To return something to its proper place.
ex: Please put away your laptops before the flight lands.
nat: She put away the groceries and made dinner.

def: To stop a fire or a cigarette from burning.
ex: Firefighters put out the fire in under an hour.
nat: Please put out your cigarette before entering.
contrast: put out (publicar): The firm put out a statement. be put out = ficar chateado.

def: To suggest an idea or plan for discussion.
ex: She put forward a new proposal at the board meeting.
nat: Several candidates were put forward for the role.

def: To assemble parts or create something from several pieces.
ex: It took us two hours to put together the new desk.
nat: Can you put together a short report by noon?

def: To leave the ground (plane); to remove clothing.
ex: The flight took off ten minutes late.
nat: Our plane will take off at noon.
contrast: take off (decolar) ; a business takes off = decola, dá certo.

def: To gain control of or responsibility for something.
ex: Maria will take over the team when Paul retires.
nat: A larger firm tried to take over the company.
contrast: take over (verbo) ≠ takeover (aquisição, substantivo).

def: To start a new hobby, or to use space or time.
ex: I took up running last year to stay healthy.
nat: This project takes up too much of my time.

def: To accept a task or responsibility, or to hire someone.
ex: She took on extra work to pay off her debt.
nat: We are planning to take on three new developers.

def: To remove something, or to obtain a loan or insurance.
ex: He took out his phone and checked the time.
nat: We need to take out a loan to buy the house.
contrast: take out a loan/insurance = contratar; take someone out = convidar para sair.

def: To return something, or to admit that something you said was wrong.
ex: I take back what I said; you were right.
nat: You can take back the shirt if it doesn't fit.

def: To resemble an older relative in appearance or character.
ex: She takes after her mother in many ways.
nat: Do you take after your dad or your mom?
contrast: take after (parente) ≠ look like (qualquer pessoa).

def: To think of an idea or plan.
ex: We need to come up with a better solution.
nat: She came up with a clever way to save time.

def: To find or meet by chance.
ex: I came across an old photo while cleaning.
nat: Have you ever come across this error before?
contrast: come across as = parecer: He comes across as shy.

def: To return to a place.
ex: When are you coming back from Rio?
nat: Come back soon; we will miss you.
contrast: come back (voltar a quem fala) ≠ go back (voltar para lá).

def: To be released, or to become known.
ex: Their new album comes out next Friday.
nat: The truth finally came out.

def: To happen unexpectedly, or to be mentioned.
ex: Sorry I am late; something urgent came up.
nat: The topic didn't come up during the interview.

def: To be the deciding factor in a situation.
ex: In the end, it comes down to price.
nat: The decision will come down to experience.

def: To continue, or to happen.
ex: Please go on; I am listening.
nat: What is going on in the meeting room?
contrast: go on + -ing = continuar fazendo; go on to + verbo = passar a fazer.

def: To check or review something carefully.
ex: Let us go over the contract before signing.
nat: I will go over your report tonight.

def: To experience something difficult, or to examine something in detail.
ex: She went through a tough time last year.
nat: Let us go through the agenda one more time.

def: To proceed with something.
ex: You can go ahead and start without me.
nat: The company decided to go ahead with the merger.
contrast: Go ahead! = pode ir em frente (dando permissão).

def: To leave home to do something social.
ex: Do you want to go out for dinner tonight?
nat: They went out together for two years.
contrast: go out (sair) ; go out with someone = namorar alguém.

def: To ring or explode, or (of food) to become bad.
ex: My alarm went off at five this morning.
nat: Be careful; the milk may go off in this heat.
contrast: go off (azedar) ; go off someone = deixar de gostar de alguém.

def: To return to a place.
ex: I would love to go back to Italy next summer.
nat: We went back to the office after lunch.
contrast: go back (voltar para lá) ≠ come back (voltar para cá).

def: To search for information in a book or online.
ex: I looked up the word in a dictionary.
nat: Can you look up the train times for me?
contrast: look up (pesquisar) ≠ look up to (admirar).

def: To take care of someone or something.
ex: Could you look after my cat while I am away?
nat: She looks after her elderly parents.
contrast: look after (cuidar) ≠ look for (procurar).

def: To feel happy about something that will happen.
ex: I look forward to hearing from you.
nat: We are looking forward to the trip.
contrast: look forward to + -ing (hearing), não + verbo base.

def: To investigate something.
ex: We will look into the problem and call you back.
nat: The police are looking into the case.

def: To watch carefully for something.
ex: Please look out for suspicious emails in your inbox.
nat: Look out for cyclists when you cross the road.
contrast: Look out! (interjeição) = Cuidado!

def: To examine something quickly.
ex: Could you look over my CV before I send it?
nat: I will look over the draft this afternoon.

def: To mention a topic, or to raise a child.
ex: She brought up the budget at the meeting.
nat: I didn't want to bring up the subject at dinner.
contrast: bring up (criar) ≠ grow up (crescer).

def: To cause something to happen.
ex: The new policy brought about major changes.
nat: Technology has brought about a revolution in education.

def: To reduce a level, or to make something fall.
ex: We need to bring down our costs this year.
nat: The attack brought down the website for hours.

def: To earn money, or to introduce something new.
ex: The new service brings in thousands of dollars a month.
nat: They plan to bring in new safety rules.

def: To return with something, or to recall a memory.
ex: Can you bring back some coffee from Brazil?
nat: That song brings back so many memories.

def: To cancel an event or plan.
ex: They called off the picnic because of the rain.
nat: The union decided to call off the strike.

def: To phone someone again.
ex: Please ask him to call back after lunch.
nat: I will call back as soon as I get the information.

def: To require, or to publicly demand something.
ex: This situation calls for immediate action.
nat: Protesters called for the minister to resign.
contrast: call for (exigir) ≠ call on (visitar/pedir a alguém).

def: To criticize someone publicly for doing something wrong.
ex: She called out her manager for ignoring the problem.
nat: Employees should feel safe to call out unfair behavior.
contrast: call out também = gritar por ajuda.

def: To solve a problem, to succeed, or to exercise.
ex: I hope everything works out for you.
nat: We finally worked out a deal with the supplier.
contrast: work out (dar certo / malhar / calcular): três sentidos comuns.

def: To spend time and effort improving or completing something.
ex: I am working on a new app this week.
nat: We need to work on our communication.

def: To find a way to deal with a problem without solving it directly.
ex: We found a temporary fix to work around the bug.
nat: Developers often work around limitations in older systems.
contrast: workaround (substantivo) = solução paliativa.

def: To deal with a problem or emotion step by step.
ex: The team worked through the issues one by one.
nat: Therapy helped her work through her anxiety.

def: To develop or build something gradually.
ex: I need to work up the courage to ask for a raise.
nat: She worked up an appetite after the hike.
contrast: get worked up = ficar nervoso, agitado.

def: To meet someone unexpectedly, or to encounter a problem.
ex: I ran into my old boss at the airport.
nat: We ran into some problems during installation.
contrast: run into (encontrar) ≠ run out of (ficar sem).

def: To have no more of something.
ex: We ran out of printer paper this morning.
nat: I am running out of time.
contrast: run out (acabar) não leva objeto: Our supplies ran out.

def: To hit someone with a vehicle, or to go beyond a time limit.
ex: The meeting ran over by twenty minutes.
nat: He nearly ran over a cyclist.

def: To rehearse, or to quickly review something.
ex: Let us run through the presentation once more.
nat: Can you run through the steps again?

def: To stop working, or to separate into parts for analysis.
ex: Our car broke down on the highway.
nat: Let us break down the costs by department.
contrast: break down também = desabar emocionalmente.

def: To end a romantic relationship.
ex: They broke up after three years.
nat: I don't want to break up with her.
contrast: break up (terminar) ≠ break down (quebrar).

def: To enter a building illegally, or to interrupt.
ex: Someone broke in and stole two laptops.
nat: Sorry to break in, but the client is on the line.

def: To start suddenly, as a fire, war or disease.
ex: A fire broke out in the warehouse last night.
nat: War broke out in 1939.

def: To force a way through, or to make an important discovery.
ex: Scientists broke through a major barrier in battery technology.
nat: The sun finally broke through the clouds.
contrast: breakthrough (substantivo) = grande avanço.

def: To invent a story, or to end an argument.
ex: He made up an excuse for being late.
nat: They argued, but they made up quickly.
contrast: make up também = compor: Women make up 60% of the staff.

def: To see or hear something with difficulty.
ex: I could barely make out the street sign in the fog.
nat: I can't make out what he is saying.
contrast: make out (distinguir) ; nos EUA, make out também = beijar (informal).

def: To compensate for something bad or missing.
ex: I will bring you dinner to make up for being late.
nat: Hard work can make up for a lack of experience.

def: To stop trying, or to stop a habit.
ex: Don't give up; you are almost there.
nat: He gave up smoking last year.

def: To finally agree or stop resisting.
ex: After hours of arguing, he gave in.
nat: Don't give in to pressure.
contrast: give in (ceder) ≠ hand in (entregar).

def: To give something for free, or to reveal a secret.
ex: We gave away our old furniture to a charity.
nat: Don't give away the ending!

def: To distribute something, or to stop working.
ex: Volunteers gave out free water during the race.
nat: My phone battery gave out halfway through the trip.

def: To continue at the same level or speed.
ex: You are doing great, so keep up the good work.
nat: Can you keep up this speed for another hour?

def: To continue doing something.
ex: He kept on talking even though nobody listened.
nat: Keep on trying; you will improve.
contrast: keep on + -ing = continuar fazendo.

def: To stay at the same level as, or informed about, something.
ex: It is hard to keep up with new technology.
nat: I walk fast to keep up with my sister.

def: To stay at a distance, or to avoid something.
ex: Please keep away from the edge of the platform.
nat: Try to keep away from sugar if you want to lose weight.

def: To collect someone or something, or to lift something.
ex: Can you pick up the kids at five?
nat: I picked up some milk on my way home.
contrast: pick up também = aprender sem esforço: pick up a language.

def: To choose or identify someone or something.
ex: She picked out a gift for her mother.
nat: Can you pick out your face in this photo?

def: To reduce the amount of something.
ex: I am trying to cut down on sugar.
nat: We should cut down our expenses.
contrast: cut down on + substantivo; cut down a tree = derrubar uma árvore.

def: To stop a supply, or to interrupt.
ex: The call was cut off halfway through.
nat: They cut off the electricity because of unpaid bills.

def: To perform or complete a task.
ex: The team carried out a detailed survey.
nat: We will carry out the tests next week.

def: To continue despite difficulty or interruption.
ex: Despite the noise, she carried on working.
nat: We will carry on the discussion tomorrow.
contrast: carry on + -ing = continuar fazendo.

def: To wait for a short time.
ex: Can you hold on for a second?
nat: Hold on tight; the road is bumpy.
contrast: hold on (esperar ao telefone) ≠ hold up (atrasar).

def: To prevent progress, or to stop yourself from showing emotion.
ex: He couldn't hold back his tears.
nat: Don't hold back; tell us what you really think.

def: To register on arrival at a hotel or airport.
ex: We checked in at the hotel at noon.
nat: You can check in online 24 hours before your flight.
contrast: check in (entrar no hotel) ≠ check out (sair do hotel).

def: To leave a hotel after paying, or to look at something interesting.
ex: Guests must check out before 11 a.m.
nat: Check out this new app; it is really useful.

def: To enter a computer system with a username and password.
ex: You need to log in to see your account.
nat: I can't log in; the password isn't working.
contrast: log in (verbo) ≠ login (substantivo): Enter your login.
